# GoWarmCRM

> The execution application for your GTM team. GoWarmCRM sits on top of Salesforce or HubSpot — or runs as the CRM for teams without one — to operationalize sales playbooks, surface deal actions, and close the gap between defined process and rep behavior. It reads behavioral signals from email, calendar, and meeting patterns — not just what reps logged — to tell teams what to do next on every deal, every morning.

GoWarmCRM has two pillars on one platform, enabled per organisation. **Sales execution** is built for B2B sales teams running multi-stage pipelines (typically SaaS, professional services, or complex field sales) with deal values above $20K, sales cycles longer than 30 days, and 5–200 reps; primary buyers are CROs, VPs of Sales, and RevOps leaders. **GoWarm Work** is project and daily work tracking for companies up to 500 people in any industry — construction, manufacturing, services, agencies, professional firms — where nobody's full-time job is keeping the record of work truthful; primary buyers are founders, CEOs and managing directors. Either pillar can run without the other.

## GoWarm CRM — sales execution
- [GoWarm CRM](https://gowarmcrm.com/sales.md): The sales execution pillar — nightly diagnostics across deals, contracts, cases, handovers and prospects, a prioritised action queue for every rep, playbooks that surface at the stage transition, and forecast health for managers and RevOps

## GoWarm Work — projects and daily work
- [GoWarm Work](https://gowarmcrm.com/work.md): The projects and daily work pillar — stages with gates, task dependencies, a baseline frozen at start, evidence required to close, Bill of Quantities with an append-only spend ledger, timeboxed versus standing work, and daily work written once by the person doing it and read by their own day, the project task and the manager rollup. Pricing: $999/month up to 25 users, custom above that; $1,499/month for both products up to 25 users
- [Why you stopped knowing what's happening in your own company](https://gowarmcrm.com/why-you-stopped-knowing.md): The argument — why status decks, weekly reviews, dashboards and project tools all report on the reporting rather than the work, why tools that generate work accumulate past the point of being read, and the three properties a record has to have to be worth trusting
- [GoWarm Work vs a shared spreadsheet](https://gowarmcrm.com/vs-spreadsheets.md): Where a shared sheet stops working: the six things a spreadsheet structurally cannot do — tell absence from silence, enforce a sequence, require evidence, aggregate free text, keep a ledger, or remember what a date used to be — what replaces each, and when the sheet is still the right answer
- [Standing versus timeboxed work](https://gowarmcrm.com/standing-vs-timeboxed-work.md): Work has two independent axes: customer or internal, and does it end. Why forcing standing work such as retainers, maintenance and compliance into a finite project shape corrupts percentage complete and overdue counts, the three common workarounds and why each fails, and how to tell the two apart
- [Project tracking software for small business](https://gowarmcrm.com/project-tracking-software-small-business.md): Why project tools fail in companies with no project office, and what replaces the administrator: gates that hold a stage shut, dependency cycle checks, a baseline frozen at start, and evidence required to close a task. Also covers standing versus timeboxed work and Bill of Quantities
- [Daily work tracking without timesheets](https://gowarmcrm.com/daily-work-tracking.md): One line a day written by the person doing the work and stored once — read on their own day, against the project task, and in the manager rollup. Controlled activity vocabulary with a manager merge queue, compliance measured against working days, and no timers, screenshots or idle detection
- [GoWarm for founders](https://gowarmcrm.com/for-founders.md): Why founders lose sight of their own company past a certain size, how the same gap runs down both the revenue and delivery sides, what changes for the founder specifically, and five diagnostic checks that cost nothing

## The AI Shift in B2B Selling — five-part thesis
- [Part 1 · The pillar](https://gowarmcrm.com/ai-shift.md): The generic thesis for B2B CEOs on why information asymmetry has collapsed, why search never broke the old motion but LLMs did, what the buyer now arrives with, the two things a seller can still uniquely provide, and why the operational response diverges sharply for product and services companies
- [Part 2 · What shifted for product companies](https://gowarmcrm.com/ai-shift/product-companies.md): The CEO-level paranoia — will someone deliver my product lighter, AI-enabled, faster? CRM as the canary for broader SaaS disruption, what compliance-as-a-service would do to incumbent moats, and the stickiness-versus-new-product decision that defines the next three years
- [Part 3 · What shifted for services companies](https://gowarmcrm.com/ai-shift/services-companies.md): The positioning crisis — people, projects, or outcomes. Why outcome-based pricing is becoming the new floor for growth-stage services firms, and why four operational shifts (account instrumentation, senior-in-delivery, continuous account farming, underwriter-sellers) have to happen in sequence, with pricing last
- [Part 4 · Marketing, sales and distribution in the AI era](https://gowarmcrm.com/ai-shift/marketing-sales-motions.md): The operational response — SEO fracturing into AEO, cold email past saturation, paid acquisition economics inverted, and the LLM-ready web as table stakes — with an eight-item audit for whether the firm's first-touch surface is LLM-readable
- [Part 5 · Relationship selling in the AI era — the synthesis](https://gowarmcrm.com/ai-shift/relationship-selling.md): Why relationship selling is not dead but being reborn, why the buyer's scarce resource has moved from information to attention, why the best sellers have always done this motion but only now can it scale, and what the integrated picture across product, services, and marketing commits the firm to on Monday morning
